**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Thank you for your contribution! Reviewed `bd06b5d16f06352e3f0debc8bc27d5b9cf4d5af1`. Keeping the handle map and mutex alive matches the lifetime required by late CUDA user-object releases. No actionable finding.

Independently reproduced the parent failure with the actual retained-resource path: both a graph left alive and a graph destroyed before `main` returns ended in SIGSEGV during static cleanup. Both cases exit cleanly with this head. A separate host-only probe isolates `get_cuda_symbol`: AddressSanitizer reports the parent's heap-use-after-free and passes on the head; 16 concurrent first-use callers also completed 160,000 lookups successfully.

Fresh native build and **79 capture/dispatch tests passed** on SM100. An interleaved warm symbol-lookup spot check showed no material CPU regression (parent medians 54.8/57.4 ns, head 54.8/54.6 ns); this is a resolver microbenchmark, not end-to-end performance evidence. The small process-lifetime allocation is intentional.

Limitations: I did not rerun the TransformerEngine suites from #1486. GPU probes under AddressSanitizer failed during CUDA initialization in both revisions, before testing teardown; the sanitizer result above is from the isolated host probe. Owner-triggered pipeline **73018245** is still running; no duplicate CI was started.
